SYSTEMS PROGRAMMING AND MACHINE ORGANIZATION
Chapter 41 — Signals
VERBATIM GRADUATE LECTURE TRANSCRIPT
Charles Dorner

SLIDE 1: Chapter 41 — Signals

LECTURE NARRATION
Signals notify a process or thread of events outside ordinary return-value control flow. They can represent terminal actions, child state changes, explicit requests, or synchronous faults. A signal handler can interrupt code at an inconvenient moment, so its safe operations are severely restricted. [ R20 , R21 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, signals notify a process or thread of events outside ordinary return-value control flow.

SLIDE 4: 41.1 Asynchronous events

LECTURE NARRATION
An asynchronous signal can arrive independently of the interrupted statement’s purpose. The program may be halfway through updating a data structure or holding a library’s internal lock. Handler code must not assume a clean application boundary. Synchronous fault signals have a different relationship to execution: they result from an instruction’s behavior. Catching such a signal does not automatically make corrupted state recoverable. Treat routine notifications and invalid-memory faults as different design problems.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, an asynchronous signal can arrive independently of the interrupted statement’s purpose.

SLIDE 6: 41.2 Signal delivery

LECTURE NARRATION
Signal disposition defines whether a signal is handled, ignored, or given its default action, subject to signals that cannot be caught or ignored. Signal masks control which signals are blocked for a thread. In a multithreaded process, dispositions and per-thread masks have different scopes. Process-directed signals can be delivered to an eligible thread under the platform’s rules. A design that depends on one particular worker receiving a signal should use a deliberate masking and signal-consumption strategy instead of leaving delivery accidental.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, signal disposition defines whether a signal is handled, ignored, or given its default action, subject to signals that cannot be caught or ignored.

SLIDE 8: 41.3 kill

LECTURE NARRATION
Despite its name, kill sends a signal; the chosen signal’s disposition determines the effect. It can request termination, notify, or test certain existence/permission conditions with signal number zero under documented rules. A PID is a reusable identifier, not an eternal object reference. Long-lived supervisors must account for lifecycle and identity races. This book’s simple examples use freshly created children or the current process rather than treating an old stored PID as permanently trustworthy.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, despite its name, kill sends a signal; the chosen signal’s disposition determines the effect.

SLIDE 10: 41.4 sigaction

LECTURE NARRATION
sigaction installs a handler and associated mask and flags. It provides explicit control that is preferable to relying on historically varying signal semantics. Initialize the structure and signal set before installing it. Flags such as SA_RESTART affect some interrupted operations, not every possible wait or system call. Correct I/O code still needs to interpret its own interface’s results. A blanket assumption that signals can never interrupt operations is unsafe.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, sigaction installs a handler and associated mask and flags.

SLIDE 12: 41.5 Signal handlers

LECTURE NARRATION
A minimal handler records that an event occurred and leaves substantial work to ordinary control flow. A volatile sig_atomic_t flag supports the limited communication pattern used here. It is not a general atomic counter or a substitute for C++ inter-thread synchronization. Do not call printf , allocate memory, acquire arbitrary mutexes, or use ordinary C++ stream operations from an asynchronous handler. They may rely on state that the interrupted code was modifying. Use only operations guaranteed async-signal-safe for the relevant environment. [ R20 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, a minimal handler records that an event occurred and leaves substantial work to ordinary control flow.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 14: 41.6 Blocking signals

LECTURE NARRATION
Blocking delays delivery; it does not necessarily discard the event. A critical setup sequence can block a signal, install state, and then unblock it at a controlled point. In multithreaded programs, use the appropriate thread-aware mask interfaces and establish masks before creating workers when that is part of the design. Blocking is also needed to close a check-then-sleep race. The signal must not slip between observing a flag and entering a wait that would then have no future notification to wake it.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, blocking delays delivery; it does not necessarily discard the event.

SLIDE 16: 41.7 Pending signals

LECTURE NARRATION
A blocked signal can become pending. Standard signals generally do not queue one distinct instance for every repeated occurrence; multiple occurrences can coalesce. Real-time signals provide different queuing semantics under their documented limits. Consequently, a handler flag is usually a request to inspect state, not an exact count of events. A SIGCHLD notification should trigger collection of all available child statuses, not one wait per presumed signal instance.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, a blocked signal can become pending.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 18: 41.8 Signal safety

LECTURE NARRATION
Signal safety concerns reentrancy and permitted operations at an asynchronous interruption point. It is not the same as ordinary thread safety. A function protected by an internal mutex can be thread-safe yet deadlock when called from a handler that interrupted a thread holding that mutex. A handler using an async-signal-safe function that can affect errno should save and restore errno when necessary. A self-pipe pattern can notify an event loop with a small write, but it must handle a full nonblocking pipe without blocking inside the handler.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, signal safety concerns reentrancy and permitted operations at an asynchronous interruption point.

========================================================================================

SLIDE 20: 41.9 Signal races

LECTURE NARRATION
A race occurs when correctness depends on the timing of delivery relative to ordinary state changes. Installing a handler after enabling an event source can miss the intended handling window. Updating shared bookkeeping without a masking plan can expose inconsistent state. Design the state transition and notification together. The signal says that something may have changed; protected ordinary code determines exactly what changed and performs the required work. This parallels condition-variable design in Part XI.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
Imagine several people editing the same whiteboard. If they do not coordinate, the final answer can depend on who writes at exactly the wrong moment.

SLIDE 22: 41.10 Sleep/wakeup races

LECTURE NARRATION
The broken pattern is if (!flag) pause(); : a signal can set the flag after the check but before pause , leaving the program asleep after the only notification. Making the flag volatile does not make those two operations atomic. sigsuspend temporarily installs a signal mask and waits as one coordinated operation. Block the relevant signal while checking the predicate, then use a mask that permits it during the wait. On return, recheck the predicate in a loop. [ R40 ]

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
Imagine several people editing the same whiteboard. If they do not coordinate, the final answer can depend on who writes at exactly the wrong moment.

SLIDE 24: Worked example — Pending delivery without a lost wakeup

LECTURE NARRATION
This deterministic demonstration blocks SIGUSR1 , raises it while blocked, and then uses sigsuspend to permit delivery. The handler only sets a flag. It does not require another process or rely on a sleep duration. Companion listing: ch41/signals.c The expected output is signal observed . The signal is already pending before the wait, yet delivery cannot be lost between the predicate check and the temporary unblocking. The example intentionally exits after demonstrating one notification; a reusable component would also restore dispositions and define a broader shutdown policy.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, this deterministic demonstration blocks SIGUSR1 , raises it while blocked, and then uses sigsuspend to permit delivery.

SLIDE 26: Worked example — Safe signal notification

LECTURE NARRATION
A signal handler should do minimal async-signal-safe work. A common pattern sets a volatile sig_atomic_t flag or writes a byte to a self-pipe, then returns. Normal code observes the flag or file descriptor and performs complex processing outside the handler. Calling arbitrary allocation or I/O library functions inside the handler can violate reentrancy requirements.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, a signal handler should do minimal async-signal-safe work.

SLIDE 28: Worked example — Closing a sleep/wakeup race

LECTURE NARRATION
If code checks ready == false and then separately goes to sleep, a signal arriving between those steps can be lost. Correct designs use an atomic blocking primitive such as sigsuspend with a carefully managed signal mask so the state check and sleep transition cannot miss the event window.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

LECTURE NARRATION

Explain what repeated standard-signal raises while blocked do and why an event counter cannot be inferred from this flag. Review 1. Why is thread-safe not equivalent to async-signal-safe? Review 2. Why does volatile not repair check-then-sleep?

SLIDE 32: Chapter Synthesis

LECTURE NARRATION
The chapter's central subject is signals. Correct reasoning requires explicit assumptions, bounds, ownership, and interface contracts. Observed behavior is evidence about a run; it is not automatically a language or system guarantee. Use the worked examples and lab to test whether the model transfers to new cases.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION

LECTURE NARRATION
Explain one mechanism from the chapter without relying on vocabulary alone. Identify one failure mode and the violated contract or invariant. State what evidence would support your diagnosis and what it would not prove. Next: Shell Architecture.

At graduate level, do not treat this as a term to memorize. Identify the contract being described, the state or representation it constrains, and the assumptions that must remain true. When this topic appears in real systems code, separate what the language guarantees from what a compiler, operating system, ABI, ISA, or particular machine happens to do. Then identify the evidence you would inspect to test the claim without overgeneralizing from a single successful run.

SIXTH-GRADE EXPLANATION
In simpler terms, explain one mechanism from the chapter without relying on vocabulary alone.
